sample_question: Why does Signal Vault say identity unresolved when I opened it from in-game?
recommended_answer: Opening the dApp proves object/game context, not player identity. Connect wallet or use the in-game access-code flow to resolve identity.

sample_question: Can I use Signal Vault without logging in?
recommended_answer: Yes. Anonymous users can view public dossiers and create local/private drafts, but cannot publish shared or tribe Signals.

sample_question: How do I log in inside the EVE Frontier in-game browser?
recommended_answer: Use the access-code fallback: connect in external browser, generate a short-lived code, enter it in the in-game browser.

sample_question: Does Signal Vault know my EVE character automatically?
recommended_answer: Not automatically in v0.1. It can resolve character after wallet/session integration using EVE/Sui data paths.
gap_or_action: Need exact implementation once EVE dApp Kit wiring is tested.

sample_question: Can someone spoof my identity by changing the URL?
recommended_answer: No. URL params are not trusted for identity. ViewerContext is resolved through session/wallet/access-code logic.

sample_question: Why does an object show as unresolved?
recommended_answer: The object type could not be verified yet. Signal Vault displays unknown safely and allows manual classification.

sample_question: Can I manually mark an object as a gate or storage unit?
recommended_answer: Yes. Manual classification is supported but visibly marked as manual/not verified.

sample_question: What does manual vs verified mean?
recommended_answer: Manual means user/tribe-classified. Verified means resolved from stronger sources like dApp Kit, GraphQL, indexer, or on-chain data.

sample_question: What if two sources disagree about object type?
recommended_answer: Signal Vault marks the entity as conflicted instead of silently overwriting one source.

sample_question: Can Signal Vault infer gate/storage/turret type from chain data?
recommended_answer: Yes, later phases add dApp Kit/GraphQL/indexer resolution. v0.1 starts manual-first with upgrade paths.
gap_or_action: Need exact resolver queries from implementation/testing.

sample_question: What is a Signal?
recommended_answer: A Signal is a typed field record attached to EVE Frontier context, such as a gate report, storage manifest, route report, or market report.

sample_question: How do I create a quick Signal in-game?
recommended_answer: Use quick action buttons on the object page such as Passed, Blocked, Permit Required, Access Denied, or Market Closed.
gap_or_action: Need final button labels from UI implementation.

sample_question: Can I edit a Signal later?
recommended_answer: Yes. Signal CRUD is in MVP scope; external mode handles deeper editing.

sample_question: What visibility levels exist?
recommended_answer: local_private, private, tribe, officer, scout_cell, and public.

sample_question: Can anonymous users create public Signals?
recommended_answer: No. Anonymous users can create local drafts/private local Signals, but publishing shared/public remote Signals requires resolved context.

sample_question: What is a dossier?
recommended_answer: A dossier is the object/system/route page that collects Signals and context for a specific EVE Frontier entity.

sample_question: What should a gate dossier show?
recommended_answer: Gate status, access/risk, last verification, recent Signals, and quick actions like Passed, Blocked, Permit Required, Hostile Nearby.

sample_question: What should a storage dossier show?
recommended_answer: Purpose, access state, manifest status, last check, warnings, and quick actions like Access Worked or Access Denied.

sample_question: Can Signal Vault track markets?
recommended_answer: Yes. Market reports can track open/closed, liquidity, trade usefulness, and hostile trade hubs.

sample_question: Can Signal Vault track systems and routes?
recommended_answer: Yes. System and route dossiers aggregate Signals about safety, gates, markets, storage, and route freshness.

sample_question: Why is my Signal stale?
recommended_answer: Signals decay based on type because intel changes. Stale means reconfirm before acting.
gap_or_action: Need exact stale timing values surfaced to users.

sample_question: Can stale Signals be deleted automatically?
recommended_answer: Current design degrades intel rather than deleting it. Auto-deletion is not specified.

sample_question: What does contradicted mean?
recommended_answer: Contradicted means recent reports disagree, such as one report saying a gate passed and another saying blocked.

sample_question: Does Signal Vault decide which report is true?
recommended_answer: Not by default. It surfaces conflict so players can re-scout or corroborate.

sample_question: What happens if I lose connection while in-game?
recommended_answer: Local-first capture stores drafts/Signals in IndexedDB/Dexie and syncs later when possible.

sample_question: Where are anonymous notes stored?
recommended_answer: Anonymous/local notes are stored locally first, not published to shared vaults.

sample_question: Can I export my notes?
recommended_answer: Yes. Import/export JSON or local backup is in v0.1/local-first scope.

sample_question: Can my tribe share Signals?
recommended_answer: Yes, but tribe vault is a later phase after identity, entities, and Signal MVP.
gap_or_action: Need final role model and integration implementation.

sample_question: Can officers have private Signals?
recommended_answer: Yes. Officer and scout-cell visibility scopes are planned.

sample_question: Can every tribe define its own trust rules?
recommended_answer: Yes in principle. Later FrontierWarden integration should support operator/tribe-controlled policy domains.

sample_question: Can Signal Vault interact with the in-game map?
recommended_answer: Initial strategy is map-aware handoff/copy/open actions, not direct control. Signal Bridge may add current-system context later.
gap_or_action: Need research/prototype against actual map APIs/tooling.

sample_question: Will this replace EF-Map?
recommended_answer: No. Signal Vault should complement map tools first, focusing on contextual memory rather than full map rendering.

sample_question: Can it detect my current system?
recommended_answer: Not in v0.1. A later Signal Bridge/log watcher may provide current-system detection.

sample_question: How does Signal Vault open from a Smart Assembly?
recommended_answer: Use in-game object routes such as /ingame/object?tenant=&itemId= or /ingame/object/:objectId configured as a dApp URL.

sample_question: Can owners set Signal Vault as a custom URL?
recommended_answer: The design assumes custom assembly URL support; implementation must verify exact sponsored transaction/config flow.
gap_or_action: Need step-by-step operator guide after testing.

sample_question: Can users see private tribe intel without logging in?
recommended_answer: No. Anonymous users only see public data. Tribe/officer/scout-cell Signals require resolved ViewerContext and permissions.

sample_question: Is manual intel safe to trust?
recommended_answer: Manual intel is useful but subjective; Signal Vault labels it clearly and separates it from verified/indexed/on-chain data.

sample_question: Does Signal Vault store wallet private keys?
recommended_answer: No. It must not store private keys, seed phrases, or wallet secrets.

sample_question: How are access codes secured?
recommended_answer: Codes are short-lived, one-time use, hashed server-side, and revocable via session controls.

sample_question: Why Vite/React instead of Next.js?
recommended_answer: Vite/React matches EVE dApp Kit and static in-game dApp needs; Next.js adds unnecessary SSR/server complexity.

sample_question: Why not build vanilla TypeScript?
recommended_answer: Vanilla could be smaller but increases integration cost with the React-first EVE dApp Kit.

sample_question: What dependencies are allowed?
recommended_answer: Dependencies must be chosen for EVE Frontier compatibility. dApp Kit is the dependency anchor.

sample_question: What is the repo structure?
recommended_answer: Use modular app/features/lib structure or monorepo-lite apps/packages separation.

sample_question: What tests are required?
recommended_answer: Typecheck, lint, unit tests, component tests, integration tests, and build must pass per phase.

sample_question: Can an AI assistant rewrite App.tsx into a giant file?
recommended_answer: No. No monolith rule: no App.tsx business logic and no files above ~400 lines without justification.

sample_question: What database schema do we use?
recommended_answer: Docs define sessions, access codes, entities, Signals, signal_entities, and audit_log tables.

sample_question: Do we use Supabase or custom API?
recommended_answer: Either Supabase or thin Hono/Fastify API. v0.1 should avoid heavy backend complexity.

sample_question: How are permissions enforced?
recommended_answer: Permission checks use ViewerContext, Signal visibility, role scopes, and server-side validation for shared reads/writes.

sample_question: What must pass before release?
recommended_answer: Typecheck, lint, tests, build, security checks, in-game route, unknown object fallback, quick capture, local storage, docs updated.

sample_question: What are the biggest project risks?
recommended_answer: Risks include in-game wallet limitations, unresolved object types, dependency drift, stale/manual intel trust, backend failure, scope creep, and permission leakage.

recommended_answer: Signal CRUD includes delete, but privacy/data retention policy is not fully documented.
